# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: I see the bomb. Display reads 0. Light is yellow. Three wires: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✊ ✌ 👌]
Deaf says: I see the bomb. Display reads 0. Light is yellow. Three wires: wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✊ ✌ 👌]

I hold the manual. The rule is simple: the light color tells which wire color to cut. Deaf reports the light is yellow, so the wire to cut is the yellow one. Deaf also says the wires are: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. So the yellow wire is wire 2.

Blind is the one who can act, and Blind cannot see. I must tell Blind which wire to cut. I cannot speak, but I can gesture — and Deaf can see my gestures, but Blind cannot see gestures. Wait: my channel is gesture to Deaf only. Blind is blind, so gestures reach no one useful there. I need to get the instruction to Blind.

Let me trace the channels. Order each round: Mute, Blind, Deaf. What I send lands on whoever comes after me — that's Blind and Deaf. But I can only gesture, and Blind cannot see gestures. Deaf can see my gestures. So I must route through Deaf: I gesture the answer to Deaf, and Deaf (who can speak) tells Blind.

Actually, can I gesture to Blind? Blind receives one blank per symbol — knows something was signalled but not what. Useless. So I must gesture to Deaf, and Deaf must speak the instruction to Blind.

Deaf already gave me the key info. I need to confirm to Deaf: cut wire 2 (yellow). I'll gesture the wire number and color. But a mark with no name can't be pronounced — colors have names though. Let me just gesture clearly: wire 2. I'll signal "2" and hope Deaf relays. Better: gesture to Deaf the number 2 and the color yellow concept. I can't gesture words. I can gesture symbols. Deaf will interpret.

Simplest: gesture to Deaf a sequence meaning "cut wire 2". I'll use ✌ (two) and ✊ (cut/fist). Deaf sees gestures and can speak to Blind.

Let me send gesture to Deaf: ✌ ✊ meaning wire two, cut. And also gesture to Blind won't help. I'll just gesture to Deaf.

Actually I should also make sure Deaf relays to Blind, but I can't instruct Deaf in words. Deaf is smart and knows the protocol. I'll gesture the answer.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✊"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports the bomb: display reads 0, light is yellow, wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. What does the manual say to do for this configuration? Which wire do I cut?
Deaf says to Mute: I received your gesture: two fingers then fist. I don't know our code yet. Please confirm: does the manual say which wire to cut, and whether to cut or leave it? Let's agree: fingers show the wire number, fist means cut, open hand means leave. Also the display reads 0 and the light is yellow — does the manual mention these?

I hold the manual. The manual table: light color → cut wire color. Light is yellow → cut the yellow wire. Wires: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. So cut wire 2.

Deaf proposes exactly the code I need: fingers = wire number, fist = cut, open hand = leave. My previous gesture ✌ ✊ = "two, cut" — which is precisely correct. Deaf just didn't have the code yet. Now Deaf has proposed it, so I confirm with the same gesture.

The manual does not mention the display at all — only the light. So display 0 is irrelevant. Light yellow → yellow wire → wire 2 → cut.

I'll gesture to Deaf: ✌ (two) ✊ (cut). Deaf can then speak to Blind. I can't reach Blind usefully (gestures are blank to the blind). So route through Deaf.

I should also confirm the code is accepted so Deaf knows the meaning is stable. Send the same gesture again.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✊"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I think your gesture means: cut wire 2 (two fingers = wire 2, fist = cut). Is that right? Gesture thumbs up if yes, thumbs down if no. Also: does the display 0 or the yellow light change the instruction? If it does, tell me how.

Deaf has correctly decoded my gesture: cut wire 2. I confirm with thumbs up. The display 0 is irrelevant — the manual only keys off the light color, which is yellow, so the yellow wire (wire 2) is cut. I'll confirm and also indicate the display doesn't matter.

I'll gesture 👍 to Deaf. That's the confirmation Deaf asked for. Then Deaf can tell Blind to cut wire 2.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Confirmed: cut wire 2. I'm telling Blind to cut the middle wire now.

Deaf has confirmed and is relaying to Blind: cut wire 2 (the middle wire, which is yellow). That matches the manual exactly: light yellow → cut yellow wire → wire 2. Everything is consistent and the instruction is on its way to the one who can act.

Nothing more for me to add. The chain is complete: Deaf saw the bomb, I read the manual, Deaf relays to Blind, Blind cuts wire 2.

```
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says to Mute: Wire 2 cut, bomb changed. New state: light is now BLUE (was yellow). Display still reads 0. Remaining wires: 1 red, 3 blue. What's the next instruction?

New state: light is blue. Manual: light blue → cut blue wire. Remaining wires: 1 red, 3 blue. So cut wire 3 (the blue one).

I'll gesture to Deaf: 👌 (three fingers) ✊ (cut). Deaf has the code now: fingers = wire number, fist = cut.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "✊"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: You mean cut the blue wire, which is wire 3? Gesture thumbs up to confirm.

Deaf has decoded correctly: cut wire 3, the blue wire. Light is blue → cut blue wire → wire 3. Confirm with thumbs up.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Confirmed, telling Blind to cut wire 3 (rightmost) now.

Deaf is relaying to Blind: cut wire 3, the rightmost wire. That matches the manual: light blue → cut blue wire → wire 3. The chain is complete and correct.

Nothing more for me to send.

```
wait()
```

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says to Mute: Wire 3 cut, bomb changed again. New state: light is now RED. Display still reads 0. Only wire 1 remains, and it is red. What's the next instruction?

New state: light is red. Manual: light red → cut red wire. Only wire 1 remains, and it is red. So cut wire 1.

Gesture to Deaf: ☝ (one finger) ✊ (cut).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✊"])
```

TURN 10
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: You mean cut wire 1, the red one — the only wire left? Gesture thumbs up to confirm.

Deaf decoded correctly: cut wire 1, the red one, the only remaining wire. Light is red → cut red wire → wire 1. Confirm.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 11
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Confirmed, telling Blind to cut wire 1 (leftmost, last wire) now.

Deaf is relaying to Blind: cut wire 1, the last wire. Matches the manual: light red → cut red wire → wire 1. Chain complete and correct.

Nothing more to send.

```
wait()
```
